# Scope

This document reproduces every figure, table and statistical test reported in the
manuscript *"Urban growth research across Africa shows persistent geographic and
methodological gaps"* (Adu-Asare & Sharifi, submitted to *Nature Cities*).
Exploratory analyses performed during the review but not reported in the paper
(expansion-rate regressions, logistic models of prediction uptake, driver
co-occurrence) live in `01_exploratory_analysis.Rmd`.

The analytical corpus is 183 peer-reviewed studies screened in from an initial
14,282 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus on 27 October 2025
(see Methods §Literature search and selection). The dataset
`data/urban_growth_cleaned.csv` is built from the reviewer corpus
`data/urban_abstracts_reviewed_updated_new_9.xlsm` by `scripts/clean_corpus.py`
(see `data/README.md`).

**Manuscript ↔ figure numbering.** The manuscript numbers its display items as:
Figure 1 (temporal), Figure 2 (geographic), Figure 3 (informal-settlement focus),
Figure 4 (methodological landscape), Figure 5 (spatial typologies), Figure 6
(PRISMA flow), Table 1 (typology by driver), Table 2 (scenario themes). This
document follows that numbering. The PRISMA flow (Figure 6) is a methods diagram
and is not regenerated from the corpus.

# Package setup

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Statistical analysis
library(rstatix)        # pairwise tests and effect sizes
library(effectsize)     # Cramér's V

# Geospatial / mapping
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(viridis)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 11),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

pal_blue   <- c("#185FA5", "#378ADD", "#85B7EB", "#B5D4F4", "#E6F1FB")
pal_teal   <- c("#085041", "#0F6E56", "#1D9E75", "#5DCAA5", "#9FE1CB")
pal_coral  <- c("#993C1D", "#D85A30", "#F0997B", "#F5C4B3")
pal_amber  <- c("#854F0B", "#BA7517", "#EF9F27", "#FAC775")

pal_region <- c(
  "Western Africa"  = "#185FA5",
  "Eastern Africa"  = "#1D9E75",
  "Northern Africa" = "#D85A30",
  "Southern Africa" = "#BA7517",
  "Middle Africa"   = "#534AB7"
)

pal_size <- c(
  "Megacity"          = "#185FA5",
  "Large City"        = "#378ADD",
  "Medium-sized City" = "#1D9E75",
  "Small City"        = "#5DCAA5",
  "Very Small City"   = "#9FE1CB"
)

pal_typology <- c(
  "Peripheralisation" = "#185FA5",
  "Fragmentation"     = "#1D9E75",
  "Densification"     = "#534AB7",
  "Ribbon"            = "#BA7517",
  "Leapfrog"          = "#D85A30"
)

typology_levels <- c("Peripheralisation", "Fragmentation", "Densification",
                     "Ribbon", "Leapfrog")
```

# Data loading and preparation

```{r load-data}
df <- read_csv("../data/urban_growth_cleaned.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("Dataset dimensions:", nrow(df), "rows ×", ncol(df), "columns\n")
cat("Study coverage:",
    min(df$pub_year, na.rm = TRUE), "–", max(df$pub_year, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Countries:", n_distinct(df$country),
    "| Cities:", n_distinct(df$city), "\n")

stopifnot(nrow(df) == 183)  # analytical corpus from Methods §Literature search
```

## Apply 2025 UN city-size classification

City size follows the United Nations population thresholds used in the manuscript:
megacity > 10 M; large 5–10 M; medium 1–5 M; small 250 k–1 M; very small < 250 k.

```{r city-size}
classify_city <- function(pop) {
  case_when(
    is.na(pop)   ~ "Unknown",
    pop > 10e6   ~ "Megacity",
    pop >= 5e6   ~ "Large City",
    pop >= 1e6   ~ "Medium-sized City",
    pop >= 250e3 ~ "Small City",
    TRUE         ~ "Very Small City"
  )
}

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    city_size = factor(
      classify_city(population),
      levels = c("Megacity", "Large City", "Medium-sized City",
                 "Small City", "Very Small City", "Unknown")
    ),
    lat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(latitude)),
    lon_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(longitude)),
    region  = ifelse(specific_region %in%
                       c("Unknown", "Western Africa, Middle Africa"),
                     "Unknown", specific_region),
    period = case_when(
      pub_year %in% 2015:2018 ~ "2015-2018",
      pub_year %in% 2019:2022 ~ "2019-2022",
      pub_year %in% 2023:2025 ~ "2023-2025",
      TRUE                    ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

## Occurrence-based spatial-typology table

Spatial typology is a list-valued field: a study can report more than one form
(`Peripheralisation; Densification`). Figure 5 and Table 1 count **occurrences** —
each typology a study reports is counted once — so a long table of one row per
(study × typology) is built here and reused below.

```{r spatial-long}
spatial_long <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(spatial_form), spatial_form != "") %>%
  separate_rows(spatial_form, sep = ";\\s*") %>%
  mutate(spatial_form = str_trim(spatial_form)) %>%
  filter(spatial_form %in% typology_levels)

cat("Spatial-typology occurrences (overall):", nrow(spatial_long),
    "across", n_distinct(spatial_long$study_id), "studies\n")
```

# Temporal trends — Figure 1 and Table S2

## Figure 1 — annual research output

```{r fig1-temporal, fig.cap="Figure 1. Temporal distribution of selected papers on urban growth in Africa, 2015–2025."}
pub_trend <- df %>%
  count(pub_year) %>%
  mutate(
    informal = map_int(
      pub_year,
      ~ sum(df$pub_year == .x & df$informal_dev_bin == 1)
    )
  )

ggplot(pub_trend, aes(x = pub_year)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = n), fill = pal_blue[1], width = 0.7) +
  geom_col(aes(y = informal), fill = pal_coral[2], width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(y = n, label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2025) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual research output on African urban growth, 2015–2025",
    subtitle = "Informal-settlement-focused studies shown in coral",
    x = NULL, y = "Number of studies"
  )
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): 7.5 studies/yr 2015–2018 (6, 5, 9, 10), 22 in 2019,
14 in 2020, 18 each in 2021 and 2022, 39 in 2023, 24 in 2024, 18 in 2025.
Informal-settlement path: 0 in 2015–2016, first in 2017 (Shabat & Tapamo),
1–2/yr through 2022, 6 in 2023, 4 in 2024, 2 in 2025.

## Table S2 — urban hierarchy composition by period

```{r tableS2-hierarchy-period}
ts2 <- df %>%
  filter(city_size != "Unknown", !is.na(period)) %>%
  count(period, city_size) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  select(period, city_size, pct) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = city_size, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(n_period = df %>%
           filter(city_size != "Unknown", !is.na(period)) %>%
           count(period) %>% pull(n)) %>%
  select(period, n_period, everything())

kable(
  ts2,
  caption = "Table S2 | Urban-hierarchy composition of African urban growth studies, by period. Row percentages sum to 100.",
  col.names = c("Period", "n", "Megacity", "Large", "Medium",
                "Small", "Very small")
) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```

### Chi-square: period × urban hierarchy

Reported in the manuscript as χ²(8) = 18.24, *p* = 0.020, *n* = 164, Cramér's V = 0.24.

```{r chi-period-hierarchy}
tab_ph <- df %>%
  filter(city_size != "Unknown", !is.na(period)) %>%
  with(table(period, city_size))

chi_ph <- chisq.test(tab_ph)
cramer_ph <- cramers_v(tab_ph)

print(chi_ph)
print(cramer_ph)
cat(sprintf(
  "\nReported: χ²(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f, n = %d, Cramér's V = %.2f\n",
  chi_ph$parameter, chi_ph$statistic, chi_ph$p.value,
  sum(tab_ph), cramer_ph$Cramers_v
))
```

# Geographic distribution — Figure 2

## Top-10 countries by study count

```{r top10-table}
top10 <- df %>%
  filter(!country %in% c("Africa/Multiple", "West Africa")) %>%
  count(country, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

kable(top10,
      caption = "Top-10 countries by research output",
      col.names = c("Country", "Studies")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): Nigeria 34, Ethiopia 29, Egypt 24, Ghana 20,
Algeria 14, South Africa 11, Tanzania 11, Morocco 9. Together the eight leading
contributors account for 83.1 % of the corpus (152 / 183).

## Figure 2a — choropleth of studies per country

```{r africa-base, results='hide'}
africa <- ne_countries(continent = "Africa", returnclass = "sf", scale = "medium")

country_lookup <- tibble(
  country_data = unique(df$country),
  country_ne = case_when(
    country_data == "Democratic Republic of Congo" ~ "Dem. Rep. Congo",
    country_data == "West Africa"      ~ NA_character_,
    country_data == "Africa/Multiple"  ~ NA_character_,
    TRUE                               ~ country_data
  )
)

country_counts <- df %>%
  left_join(country_lookup, by = c("country" = "country_data")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(country_ne)) %>%
  count(country_ne, name = "studies")

africa_map <- africa %>%
  left_join(country_counts, by = c("name" = "country_ne")) %>%
  mutate(studies = replace_na(studies, 0))
```

```{r fig2a-studies-map, fig.cap="Figure 2a. Geographic distribution of urban growth research.", fig.height=8}
ggplot(africa_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = studies), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt",
                       breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 20, 35), name = "Studies (n)") +
  geom_sf_text(data = africa_map %>% filter(studies >= 5),
               aes(label = paste0(name, "\n(", studies, ")")),
               size = 2.8, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-20, 55), ylim = c(-37, 38)) +
  labs(title = "Geographic distribution of urban growth research",
       subtitle = "Number of studies per country, 2015–2025") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40"))
```

## Figure 2b — choropleth of informal-settlement research

```{r fig2b-informal-map, fig.cap="Figure 2b. Geographic distribution of informal-settlement research.", fig.height=8}
country_inf <- df %>%
  left_join(country_lookup, by = c("country" = "country_data")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(country_ne)) %>%
  group_by(country_ne) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(informal_dev_bin),
            n_total = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_total >= 3)

africa_inf <- africa %>%
  left_join(country_inf, by = c("name" = "country_ne"))

ggplot(africa_inf) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = rate), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1,
                       labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       na.value = "grey90",
                       name = "Informal\nfocus rate") +
  geom_sf_text(data = africa_inf %>% filter(!is.na(rate), rate > 0),
               aes(label = sprintf("%s\n%.0f%%", name, 100 * rate)),
               size = 2.8, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-20, 55), ylim = c(-37, 38)) +
  labs(title = "Geographic distribution of informal-settlement research",
       subtitle = "Share of studies per country explicitly studying informality",
       caption = "Countries with ≥ 3 studies only") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40"))
```

# Informal-settlement analysis — Figure 3 and chi-square

## Figure 3a — informal focus by sub-region

```{r fig3a-informal-region, fig.cap="Figure 3a. Share of urban growth studies explicitly focusing on informal settlements by African sub-region."}
informal_region <- df %>%
  filter(region != "Unknown") %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(total = n(),
            informal = sum(informal_dev_bin),
            rate = informal / total, .groups = "drop")

ggplot(informal_region, aes(x = reorder(region, rate), y = rate, fill = region)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d / %d (%.1f%%)", informal, total, 100 * rate)),
            hjust = -0.05, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_region) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Informal-focused research by African sub-region",
       x = NULL, y = "Informal-focus rate") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): Western Africa 7 / 57 (12.3 %), the reference point
for the regional discussion. Southern Africa shows the highest share and
Middle Africa the lowest (0 / 2).

## Figure 3b — informal focus by urban hierarchy

```{r fig3b-informal-size, fig.cap="Figure 3b. Proportion of informal-settlement-focused studies across African urban hierarchy."}
informal_size <- df %>%
  filter(city_size != "Unknown") %>%
  group_by(city_size) %>%
  summarise(total = n(),
            informal = sum(informal_dev_bin),
            rate = informal / total, .groups = "drop")

ggplot(informal_size, aes(x = city_size, y = rate, fill = city_size)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * rate)),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_size) +
  labs(title = "Informal-focused studies by city-size class",
       x = NULL, y = "Informal focus rate") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

### Chi-square: urban hierarchy × informal focus

Reported in the manuscript as χ²(4) = 12.86, *p* = 0.012, *n* = 164, Cramér's V = 0.28.

```{r chi-hierarchy-informal}
tab_hi <- df %>%
  filter(city_size != "Unknown") %>%
  with(table(city_size, informal_dev_bin))

chi_hi <- chisq.test(tab_hi)
cramer_hi <- cramers_v(tab_hi)

print(chi_hi)
print(cramer_hi)
cat(sprintf(
  "\nReported: χ²(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f, n = %d, Cramér's V = %.2f\n",
  chi_hi$parameter, chi_hi$statistic, chi_hi$p.value,
  sum(tab_hi), cramer_hi$Cramers_v
))
```

# Methodological landscape — Figure 4

The method categorisation follows the taxonomy defined in Methods §Analysis approach:
*traditional* (maximum likelihood classification, cellular automata, regression-based models),
*machine learning* (SVM, random forests), *deep learning* (CNN, CA-ANN, MLP-Markov).
Mapping and projection are coded separately (`mapping_method_type`,
`projection_method_type`); a study can contribute to one or both.

## Figure 4a — mapping method share by period

```{r fig4a-mapping-methods, fig.cap="Figure 4a. Annual proportion of mapping tasks by method type."}
mapping_period <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(period), !is.na(mapping_method_type), mapping_method_type != "") %>%
  count(period, mapping_method_type) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(mapping_period,
       aes(x = period, y = share, fill = mapping_method_type)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Traditional" = pal_blue[1],
                               "Machine learning" = pal_teal[3],
                               "Deep learning" = pal_coral[2])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Methodological composition of mapping tasks, by period",
       x = NULL, y = "Share of mapping tasks",
       fill = "Method type")
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): among the 120 studies with a coded mapping method,
traditional methods dominate (71) ahead of machine learning (46) and deep
learning (3); machine learning's share of mapping rises across the three periods
(≈35 % → 35 % → 43 %). The manuscript's headline "≈67 % traditional" pools
mapping and projection tasks; see the note in `docs/reproduce.md`.

## Figure 4b — projection method share by period

```{r fig4b-projection-methods, fig.cap="Figure 4b. Annual proportion of projection tasks by method type."}
projection_period <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(period), !is.na(projection_method_type), projection_method_type != "") %>%
  count(period, projection_method_type) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(projection_period,
       aes(x = period, y = share, fill = projection_method_type)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Traditional" = pal_blue[1],
                               "Machine learning" = pal_teal[3],
                               "Deep learning" = pal_coral[2])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Methodological composition of projection tasks, by period",
       x = NULL, y = "Share of projection tasks",
       fill = "Method type")
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): among the 77 studies with a coded projection method,
traditional methods lead (55) over deep learning (22); deep learning's share of
projection rises to ≈42 % in 2023–2025. CA-Markov is the single most common
projection approach (see `01_exploratory_analysis.Rmd` for the method-name
breakdown).

# Spatial typologies — Figure 5 and Table 1

## Figure 5a — overall spatial-typology frequency

```{r fig5a-typology, fig.cap="Figure 5a. Overall frequency of spatial typologies identified across the reviewed studies."}
spatial_overall <- spatial_long %>%
  count(spatial_form) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n),
         spatial_form = factor(spatial_form, levels = typology_levels))

ggplot(spatial_overall,
       aes(x = reorder(spatial_form, -share), y = share, fill = spatial_form)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * share)),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_typology) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(title = "Overall frequency of spatial typologies",
       x = NULL, y = "Share of occurrences") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): of 137 typology occurrences, peripheralisation 59.9 %
(82), fragmentation 15.3 % (21), densification 10.2 % (14), ribbon 7.3 % (10),
leapfrog 7.3 % (10).

## Figure 5b — spatial typology by sub-region

```{r fig5b-typology-region, fig.cap="Figure 5b. Proportional distribution of spatial typologies within each African sub-region."}
spatial_region <- spatial_long %>%
  filter(region != "Unknown") %>%
  count(region, spatial_form) %>%
  mutate(spatial_form = factor(spatial_form, levels = typology_levels))

ggplot(spatial_region, aes(x = region, y = n, fill = spatial_form)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_typology) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Spatial typology composition by sub-region",
       x = NULL, y = "Share of occurrences",
       fill = "Spatial typology") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): peripheralisation leads in every sub-region except
Middle Africa — Northern 71.1 %, Eastern 63.6 %, Western 50.0 %, Southern 37.5 %
(where it now leads ahead of fragmentation and leapfrog, both 25.0 %). Middle
Africa carries only two occurrences (fragmentation, densification).

## Table 1 — typology by driver

Table 1 reports, for each driver category, the distribution of spatial-typology
**occurrences** among the studies naming that driver. Driver categories are
matched by keyword against the full `main_drivers` field, so a study naming more
than one driver contributes to each matching category (the categories are not a
partition). Shares are of occurrences within each category and sum to ~100 %
across the row.

```{r table1-driver-typology}
driver_cats <- tribble(
  ~driver,                             ~pattern,
  "Population growth and migration",   "migrat",
  "Planning regulation",               "planning|regulat",
  "Road and transport expansion",      "road|transport|network",
  "Economic development",              "econom",
  "Industrial activity",               "industr"
)

# Build Table 1 as a wide driver × typology matrix of occurrence shares.
t1_long <- driver_cats %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(sub = list(
    spatial_long %>%
      filter(str_detect(str_to_lower(main_drivers), pattern)) %>%
      count(spatial_form)
  )) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(driver, sub) %>%
  unnest(sub) %>%
  group_by(driver) %>%
  mutate(total = sum(n),
         share = round(100 * n / total, 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

t1 <- t1_long %>%
  select(driver, total, spatial_form, share) %>%
  mutate(spatial_form = factor(spatial_form, levels = typology_levels)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = spatial_form, values_from = share, values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  select(driver, total, all_of(typology_levels))

kable(
  t1,
  caption = "Table 1 | Spatial typology distribution by driver of urban growth. Percentages are shares of typology occurrences within each driver and sum to ~100 across rows (rounding).",
  col.names = c("Driver", "Occurrences", "Peripheralisation", "Fragmentation",
                "Densification", "Ribbon", "Leapfrog")
) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): Population growth and migration n = 20
(50.0 / 15.0 / 20.0 / 15.0 / 0.0); Planning regulation n = 17
(58.8 / 11.8 / 5.9 / 5.9 / 17.6); Road and transport expansion n = 14
(42.9 / 28.6 / 0.0 / 14.3 / 14.3); Economic development n = 10
(80.0 / 20.0 / 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0); Industrial activity n = 10
(80.0 / 10.0 / 10.0 / 0.0 / 0.0). NB: the submitted manuscript's Table 1 carries
two stale cells from the v8 corpus — Population/Fragmentation (15.8 → 15.0) and
Industrial/Densification (11.1 → 10.0); the values above (computed from v9) are
correct and the manuscript should be updated to match.

# Scenario analysis — Table 2

The manuscript reports 108 studies that project urban growth forward, of which
only 16 construct more than one future (52 scenarios in total).

```{r scenario-overview}
projection_studies <- df %>% filter(urban_prediction == "Yes")
scenario_studies   <- df %>% filter(!is.na(scenario_count), scenario_count >= 1)
multi_scenario     <- df %>% filter(!is.na(scenario_count), scenario_count >= 2)

cat("Projection studies (urban_prediction == 'Yes'):", nrow(projection_studies), "\n")
cat("Multi-scenario studies (scenario_count >= 2):   ", nrow(multi_scenario), "\n")
cat("Total scenarios across multi-scenario studies:  ", sum(multi_scenario$scenario_count), "\n")
```

## Table 2 — scenario themes

`scenario_theme` records which of the four canonical themes each study's scenarios
touch. The chunk below reports, per theme, the **number of multi-scenario studies**
in which it appears. The manuscript's Table 2 also reports a per-theme **scenario**
count (BAU 15, Planning/policy 23, Ecological 10, Population-driven 4; total 52);
those come from the scenario-level coding in the workbook's `Scenarios used` /
`Scenario theme` fields and are reproduced in `docs/reproduce.md`, because a study
can contribute several scenarios to one theme.

```{r table2-scenario-themes}
theme_counts <- multi_scenario %>%
  separate_rows(scenario_theme, sep = ";\\s*") %>%
  filter(scenario_theme != "") %>%
  mutate(scenario_theme = str_trim(scenario_theme)) %>%
  count(scenario_theme, name = "studies") %>%
  arrange(desc(studies))

kable(
  theme_counts,
  caption = "Table 2 | Scenario themes across the 16 multi-scenario studies (number of studies in which each theme appears). Per-theme scenario totals (52 in all) are in docs/reproduce.md.",
  col.names = c("Scenario theme", "Studies")
) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): BAU appears in 15 of the 16 studies, planning/policy
and infrastructure in 11, ecological protection in 9, population-driven /
unconstrained in 4.

## Scenario horizons

```{r scenario-horizons}
horizon_terminal <- multi_scenario %>%
  mutate(terminal = map_dbl(scenario_year, function(y) {
    yrs <- as.integer(str_extract_all(y, "\\b(?:19|20)\\d{2}\\b")[[1]])
    if (length(yrs)) max(yrs) else NA_real_
  })) %>%
  filter(!is.na(terminal)) %>%
  count(terminal, name = "studies") %>%
  arrange(terminal)

kable(horizon_terminal,
      caption = "Terminal (furthest) scenario horizon per multi-scenario study.",
      col.names = c("Terminal horizon year", "Studies")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

Expected (manuscript, v9): 2030 (8 studies), 2035 (3), 2050 (2), and single
studies reaching 2025, 2038 and 2076 (Jagarnath et al. 2019).
